_comment: What an @UVRANGE growth rule can work out, write and show: the one list both runtimes use.
php/GrowthOutputs.php reads this file; tests/gen_mode_registry.cjs writes the engine's copy into js/engine.js
(the @generated growth-outputs block) and CI fails when that copy is stale.
A key is an output id, or an id, a colon and a parameter when the entry has "param": valueAtZ:-2, valueAtPercentile:97.
written: number or text. places: the decimals a number, or the numbers in a text, are written with: z (always 2), decimals (the rule's
"decimals"), percentileDecimals (the rule's "percentileDecimals"), axis (the axis value, to at most two decimals, with no
trailing zeros) or typed (the measurement as it was typed). integer: a number written with 0 decimals may go
into an integer field. needs: what the value is made from besides the sex and the age or length: measurement
(the typed value), limit-low, limit-high, limit-any (the rule's limits on that side), or none.
param: the parameter's meaning, its range (both ends included) and the most decimals it may have.
shapes: where the output may appear: value is one field of "return", column a column of the page table ("show" "table"
"columns"), line a curve of the growth chart ("show" "chart" "lines"). line: for an output with the line shape, the key
"lines" names it by, such as {"z":[-2,0,2]}. unit: the unit a column's header names: measure (the measured field's),
axis (the reference's axis unit), or none when the key is left out.
example: a field name the parser suggests; {param} stands for the parameter, - written m and . written _.
label: the English name of the output, the default table header: {param} stands for the parameter, {measure} for what the
reference measures (weight) and {axis} for its axis (age, length or height). Every id must be one GrowthReference::COMPUTED
